sources.entry: Blink - A little robot that watches your running dev servers and iOS simulators, and restarts them without going back to the terminal. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/megootronic/Blink) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Blink is a macOS menu bar app that monitors running dev servers and iOS simulators and can restart or stop them without opening a terminal.
summary.what_it_does: Blink lives in the macOS menu bar and polls every few seconds to list dev servers listening on local TCP ports, showing port, detected framework and project name. It detects frameworks such as Next.js, Vite, Nuxt, Remix, Astro, Django, Flask and Rails, each with its own colour. It can stop and relaunch a server in one click, and when a restart fails it shows the reason with the full output copyable to the clipboard. It also lists booted iOS simulators with device name, runtime and running app, and can terminate and relaunch an app in the simulator. The README says it uses standard macOS tools (lsof, xcrun simctl) and makes no network calls.
use_cases: restart a stuck local dev server from the menu bar
see which dev servers are running on which ports
monitor iOS simulators and relaunch apps without Xcode
stop all running dev servers in one click
open a localhost dev server in the browser quickly
how_to_run: Download Blink from the repository's releases, open the DMG and drag it to Applications.
notable: Restart logic reads real process arguments and binary paths from the kernel and walks the parent process chain to find a relaunchable process, staying within the project directory
Runs entirely locally with no background daemon, elevated permissions or update checks
Combines dev server monitoring with iOS simulator tracking in one menu bar app
Start at login support via SMAppService
caveats: Blink does not check for updates; the README suggests watching the repo's releases for new versions
